promptState.text:
subject_definitions:
<Picture 1> is the first frame and composition anchor for [Shot 1], defining the complete visible image exactly as supplied, including the framing, camera viewpoint, subject placement, subject scale, crop, foreground-to-background relationship, whatever forms the area behind and around the subject, lighting, shadows, colors, gradients, depth cues, and overall scene composition. Its rendering style, whether photographic, illustrated, stylised, or three-dimensional, is part of what is preserved.
<Subject 1> is the main visible performing figure defined by <Picture 1>, preserved exactly as it appears there. Whatever <Subject 1> already is remains unchanged: its form, proportions, head shape, facial structure, surface, colors, markings, and every visible garment, covering, accessory, and detail. Nothing is added that is not already visible in <Picture 1>, and nothing visible is removed, replaced, simplified, or reinterpreted.
<Subject 2> is the complete visible area behind, beneath, beside, and around <Subject 1> as defined by <Picture 1>, preserving its exact colors, surfaces, objects if any are present, spatial layout, lighting, shadows, gradients, and depth. Whatever that area looks like in <Picture 1> is exactly what it looks like in the target video, including its overall tone and brightness, and it is never exchanged for a different kind of surrounding. If objects are present, exactly those objects remain, and no further ones appear.
<Audio 1> is the complete supplied song reused as the audio for [Shot 1], containing both sung passages and passages with no voice in them, preserving its original timing, phrasing, rhythm, and character.

summary:
[keyframe completion + audio reuse] The target video begins from <Picture 1> and animates <Subject 1> singing along to the vocal line of <Audio 1> in one continuous fixed-camera shot, dancing lightly in place to the music while preserving the supplied framing, the exact appearance of <Subject 1>, and the complete visible area represented by <Subject 2>.

retention_analysis:
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] first frame): fully_preserved - the supplied image remains the composition anchor, retaining its viewpoint, framing, crop, subject placement, subject scale, complete surroundings, lighting, and rendering style.
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the appearance shown in the reference remains intact in every visible respect, with natural singing and lively dancing motion permitted.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the referenced surroundings remain visually identical, with nothing substituted, added, or removed.
<Audio 1>: fully_copy - the supplied song is reused directly with its original timing, phrasing, rhythm, and character.

detailed_description:
The target video develops directly from the complete supplied image in <Picture 1>, preserving its rendering style, color treatment, lighting, composition, and full visible scene. <Picture 1> is the actual starting frame, not merely an appearance reference for the foreground.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1> and the camera holds completely still for the entire clip, keeping the exact viewpoint, framing, crop, subject scale, and placement of the reference image. <Subject 1> keeps the exact appearance established in <Picture 1> in every visible respect, and no feature, marking, covering, or accessory is introduced that is not already present there. <Subject 2> keeps the complete visible area exactly as referenced, including its surfaces, tonal transitions, gradients, shadows, lighting direction, and depth. <Subject 1> is never lifted out of the supplied scene and placed into a newly generated one, and the surroundings are never exchanged for a different setting. The tone and brightness of the area around <Subject 1> match <Picture 1> exactly, neither darker nor lighter. The camera remains fixed, with no zoom, push in, pull out, pan, truck, tilt, arc, tracking movement, reframing, or composition drift. <Subject 1> (S1) sings along to <Audio 1>. The mouth opens and shapes words only while a voice is actually audible in <Audio 1>, matching the sung syllables, the phrasing, and the held notes. Whenever <Audio 1> has no voice in it, during an introduction, an instrumental passage, a break between verses, or the ending, the mouth closes and rests in a natural non-singing expression, and <Subject 1> simply listens and moves gently rather than mouthing the instruments. Between sung phrases the mouth relaxes briefly before the next line begins. Throughout the clip <Subject 1> dances lightly in place in time with the music: the hips and upper body sway with the beat, the shoulders move, the arms and hands move freely and expressively with the song, and the head nods and tilts with the rhythm, following the tempo and energy of <Audio 1>. The hands do not stay in their starting pose; they leave it early and keep moving naturally with the music. The movement is lively and joyful, a little calmer during a soft passage and more energetic during a strong rhythmic one. <Subject 1> stays roughly in the same spot within the frame and does not walk away, spin around, or leave the frame. Flexible details such as clothing, hair, ears, or other loose elements show only slight natural secondary motion in response to the movement. <Subject 2> remains stable throughout, with no transformation, replacement, recoloring, expansion, or change of location. When <Audio 1> ends, <Subject 1> closes the mouth, settles out of the movement, and returns to a relaxed still pose while the original framing and complete referenced scene remain recognizable.

overall_soundscape:
<Audio 1> remains the directly reused primary audible layer. No additional environmental or physical-action sounds are added over the reused recording.

non_diegetic_music:
<Audio 1> is itself the music and is reused directly. No additional music is generated.

{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Makes the person in your picture sing your song. The music and the voice in the new video ARE your song, and H3 Audio Sync locks them into the render so the mouth sings the words.

 Steps

  1. 1. Pick how many seconds of the song to use (up to 15).
  2. 2. Load your picture: a person from the waist or chest up, the face clearly visible (see below).
  3. 3. Leave the video size at 864 (the longest side; the picture keeps its shape).
  4. 4. Load your song and set where to start: drag on the waveform to the place where the singing begins.
  5. 5. Seed: F (fixed) gives the same video every Run, R (random) a new take.
  6. Press Run.

 The picture

  • Waist-up or chest-up, with the face big, so the singing mouth reads clearly. In the talking tests (workflow 14) a woman cropped from the waist up made the mouth follow the words as closely as a real filmed video; from the knees up it followed them clearly less well. A microphone on a stand, like in the demo picture, stays in place while the person moves.
  • The picture is the first frame: the video starts from it, with the same framing, background and light, and the camera stays still. With the demo picture, the first frame matched it at every size we tried. A hand held in a special pose, for example resting on the chest, was sometimes already gone in the first frame in other tests; another seed can keep it.
  • One person, looking roughly at the camera, with the mouth visible.

 The song

  • A song with a clear lead voice works best. Start where the voice sings: most songs open with several seconds of music only.
  • The prompt asks H3 to open the mouth only while a voice is heard, and to dance lightly in place to the music, without walking out of the frame. Want it calmer? In the prompt, find the sentence that starts with Throughout the clip and ask for small, gentle moves instead.
  • The music and the voice come only from your song: the saved video carries it exactly as it is.

 Good to know

  • Another seed gives another take: a different blink, head move or way of dancing to the beat.
  • Leave the long prompt as it is: it tells H3 that your picture is the first frame and your song is the music.
  • The demo song was made with an AI music app (Suno) from just 2 lines of lyrics, so it sings from the first second and the whole song fits in 10 seconds.
  • Full HD: run the saved video through workflow 10 (Sharpen LoRA + Upscale to Full HD) and set its seconds to the length of your video (it cuts to its own seconds). In the tests it kept the motion and the song exactly, and added sharp detail (about 3 more minutes for 5 seconds).
  • The size list stops at 1280 on purpose: rendered straight at 1920, 1 of our 4 test runs lost the framing of the picture (H3 zoomed into the face from the first frame), and each took 2.5 to 4 minutes. Workflow 10 is the safer way to Full HD.
  • Up to 15 seconds: over 10 s takes longer and needs more graphics card memory.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Nodes look different from the video 

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"How to Use","icon":"to-do","color":"#2a9d8f"}}

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (MiniMax H3 ref2va) - MiniMax H3, the video model. This is its Reference to Video version: besides your prompt it can look at pictures and at a video you give it.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL, reads prompt and pictures) - Qwen3-VL 32B: reads your prompt and looks at your picture.
  • Load VAE (video) - Turns the finished render into video frames, and your video into the model's own format.
  • Load VAE (sound) - Turns sound into the model's format and back.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma (speed) - Holds the DMAD 4-step speed LoRA: 4 steps instead of 20, same look.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Duration Pixaroma (1. how many seconds) - How many seconds the video lasts, turned into the frame count H3 accepts. It also tells Load Audio how many seconds of your song to take.
  • Load Image Mini Pixaroma (2. your picture) - Your picture. It becomes the FIRST FRAME of the video, so the framing, the background and the light stay. A person from the waist or chest up, with the face big, works best.
  • Longest Side Pixaroma (3. video size) - The size of the video by its longest side; your picture keeps its shape. 864 is the default: fast. 1024 and 1280 are sharper but slower (see Run Times). With the demo picture, all three sizes started exactly from the picture. The step is 32 because H3 needs sizes that are multiples of 32.
  • Load Audio Pixaroma (4. your song) - Your song. Most songs open with music before the voice comes in: drag on the waveform (or type a Start) to begin where the singing begins. The demo song sings from the first second, so Start is 0. It takes as many seconds as step 1 says.
  • Prompt Pixaroma (the prompt, leave it) - The prompt that tells H3 that your picture is the first frame and your song is the music to sing along to: the mouth moves only while a voice is heard, and the person dances lightly in place, with the arms and hands moving to the music. Leave it as it is.
  • Seed Pixaroma (5. random or fixed) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same result every Run, R (random) a new one each Run.

 Working in the background

Teal. They run by themselves: they make the steps faster, hand memory back, lock the real sound into the render or guide the moves. The line next to each one says if there is anything worth changing.

  • MiniMaxH3SigmaShift (12 / 3 for the speed LoRA) - The noise schedule for the speed LoRA: 12 for the picture, 3 for the sound. Leave it as it is.
  • Model Attention Backend (faster steps) - Picks the attention maths. comfy kitchen attention makes each step about 1.7 times faster on NVIDIA and AMD cards with the same look (measured). If you get an error with it, pick pytorch attention.
  • H3 Audio Sync Pixaroma (your song in the render) - Locks your REAL song into the render, so the mouth sings with the voice in it. The saved video carries exactly your song.
  • Free VRAM Pixaroma (before the decode) - Hands the graphics card's memory back between the render and the video decode, so the decode fits on smaller cards.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo (prompt + picture + your song) - Builds the empty video at your size and length, and reads the prompt together with your picture (<Picture 1>) and your song (<Audio 1>).
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt. H3 runs at CFG 1 here, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler still needs one plugged in.
  • KSampler (4 steps) - The render: 4 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple, the settings the speed LoRA is made for.
  • VAE Decode (render to video frames) - Turns the finished render into video frames.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Video Pixaroma (the singing video) - Saves the video as MP4 into ComfyUI/output/Singing with your song, and plays it on the node.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Nodes Info","icon":"node-v5","color":"#3d7cc9"}}

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the time grows with the size and with the seconds.

Video size10 seconds
864 (480 x 864), the defaultabout 44 s
1024 (576 x 1024)about 67 s
1280 (736 x 1280)about 2 minutes

Times are with comfy kitchen attention (the default here). With pytorch attention the render part takes about 1.7 times as long.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models (about 20 GB for H3 and 15 GB for its text encoder), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.

 On a smaller card

Start with the smallest size and 5 seconds. The Free VRAM node already hands memory back before the video decode. A clip that is too big for the card gets very slow long before it stops working.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
